accuracy_window.momentum_feasibility: A strict open choice exists when max(M_*,p_max/epsilon^(1/6)) < Lambda_p; choose p_UV inside that interval and gamma=(M_*/p_UV)^6.

low_energy_cutoff_map.target_speed_inversion: For z=alpha/(2-alpha), desired C=c_s^2 requires ell=2C alpha/[2-alpha(1+3C)] when denominator>0.

design_rule: Choose the phenomenological M_* and c_s together with alpha,ell and gamma so that the exact BPS cutoffs satisfy max(M_*,p_max/epsilon^(1/6)) < p_UV < Lambda_p and sqrt(2)c_s M_* < Lambda_omega. Gamma is then fixed by p_UV through gamma=(M_*/p_UV)^6.
interpretation: The two-crossover BPS route can in principle be made RTK-accurate on a finite momentum band while activating z=3 scaling before the published low-energy BPS momentum/frequency strong-coupling scales. The available window is quantitative and falsifiable rather than qualitative.
remaining_C8_work: identify/map the intended RTK phenomenological M_* and c_s into the BPS candidate
choose an explicit p_max and accuracy epsilon relevant to the observable/EFT domain
verify the inequalities numerically or parametrically at that target point
specialize the full selected-family cubic and higher-spatial interaction vertices and canonical normalization
check that no tuned higher-spatial coefficient generates a lower interaction cutoff than the low-energy BPS estimate
non_claims: not a numerical strong-coupling cutoff for the final RTK theory
not proof that all selected-family nonlinear vertices are weakly coupled
not full C7 nonlinear DOF closure
not radiative stability or a UV-completion proof
